channel.title: FT – Fiction
channel.description: Fiction reviews and articles from the Financial Times.

item.title: Élisabeth by Éric Rohmer — the novel that foretold the films
item.description: Newly translated, the director’s 1946 story of flirting, swimming and bickering in the French countryside heralds the screen classics to come

item.title: The best books of the week
item.description: From democracy in peril to Putin’s Russia, Hockney and Guardiola. Plus: Paul Yoon’s modern parable of war, Irvine Welsh and Claudia Rankine on Trump’s America — and our science fiction round-up

item.title: Irvine Welsh’s Can Nothing Save Us? — a family at war in Maga America
item.description: The ‘Trainspotting’ author’s well-rounded cast tell a story of envy, violence and generational conflict against the backdrop of Trump’s presidency

item.title: Etna by Paul Yoon — the horrors of war through a dog’s eyes
item.description: The brutal world of a battle-weary canine narrator is a piercing classic of survival with the feel of a modern parable

item.title: Sky City by Jacqueline Crooks — tuning into trauma
item.description: Pirate radio offers solace for a troubled young north London woman in the follow-up to Crooks’s acclaimed debut, ‘Fire Rush’

item.title: Possession — Jamaica-set thriller confronts the ghosts of the past
item.description: Gugu Mbatha-Raw leads this ambitious inheritance-dispute drama which takes on the legacy of colonialism

item.title: Jacaranda by Gaël Faye — after the genocide
item.description: An award-winning novel moves between France and Rwanda to explore a national trauma through exile, silences and family secrets

item.title: Good aliens, bad aliens and wisecracking wisdom — the best new science fiction books
item.description: YouTuber Sam A Miller reworks ‘Flowers for Algernon’ in a debut collection of future tales, while rebel groups hold out after Earth is invaded in ‘The Peace Child’

item.title: Middlemen by Laura B McGrath — literature’s power brokers
item.description: An insider’s look at publishing argues that literary agents have shaped genres, global reputations and the economics of modern fiction

item.title: Where Are the Kings — Donal Ryan’s soul-piercing novel of adolescent grief
item.description: In his story of a family wracked by loss, the prizewinning Irish author’s incisive prose and flashes of humour keep mawkish sentiment in check

item.title: The Old Man by the Sea — memory and make-believe merge in a beachside stroll
item.description: Award-winning Italian author Domenico Starnone’s elegantly translated novel is a mischievous blurring of past and present

item.title: Great Granny Webster — Caroline Blackwood’s twisted, aristocratic fairy tale
item.description: This Booker-shortlisted 1977 novel, now reissued by Virago Modern Classics, reads like a memoir refracted through gothic fantasy

item.title: Top chills, gritty thrills and sailing with serial killers — best new crime mysteries
item.description: Eight twisty tales from Yrsa Sigurðardóttir, AA Dhand, Kate Rhodes, David Heska Wanbli Weiden and more

item.title: Born of Guilt — the heavy baggage of migration
item.description: In Joanna Elmy’s award-winning debut novel, moving from post-communist Bulgaria to the US fails to upend the hardship a young woman’s life

item.title: Château Rouge — Amit Chaudhuri’s vivid vignettes of living in Paris
item.description: In a non-linear novel ripe with wit and writerly ambition, profound insights emerge amid evocations of the prosaic

item.title: How to Make a Woman — a tale of two friendships, heartbreakingly observed
item.description: Perceptive and poignant, Marie Darrieussecq’s novel traces the diverging lives of two female friends from childhood to adulthood

item.title: Children of Wolves — a thrilling tangle of scheming and sexual tension in Istanbul
item.description: Lawrence Osborne’s atmospheric page-turner is a tale of sleuthing, rebellious rich kids and darker truths

item.title: Earth 7 — an eccentric, comic elegy for a dying planet
item.description: Deb Olin Unferth’s sci-fi novel is a wild ride through time and space — and a love story for a broken world

item.title: Beginning Middle End — memory, motherhood and starting over
item.description: A shape-shifting sea god anchors Valeria Luiselli’s impressive, searching novel of broken families and second chances

item.title: Passage by Colin Thubron — a mesmerising exploration of marriage and the mind
item.description: Set in the Valley of the Kings, this haunting novel shows the writer at the summit of his powers

item.title: Cool Machine — Colson Whitehead’s Harlem trilogy reaches its reckoning
item.description: The writer powerfully uses crime fiction to explore Black aspiration, family loyalty and the forces that reshaped New York from the civil rights era to Reaganomics

item.title: Best new thrillers — a journalist in peril, a spy in WW1 and thrills of the chase
item.description: Charles Cumming returns with his Box 88 series, an impressive debut from Connor Martin in ‘The Silver Fish’ and more

item.title: It Will Come Back to You by Sigrid Nunez — tales from her brilliant career
item.description: Perceptive, funny and unsettling, a collection of short stories from the writer of ‘The Friend’ shows the emergence of her distinctive voice

item.title: The Past Pursues Us Like Detectives, Debt Collectors, Thieves — a noir tale of small-town Mexico
item.description: Juan Pablo Villalobos’s unsettling sixth novel blurs fact and fiction, and past and present in a setting where crime hovers at the fringes

item.title: Red Sheet — James Ellroy’s lacerating, liberal-baiting vision of McCarthyite America
item.description: Set in 1962 Los Angeles, the follow-up to ‘The Enchanters’ is a mesmerising crime thriller full of corruption, cynicism and sleaze
